Python: species names

Source: vignettes/articles/python-names.Rmd
python-names.Rmd

Reading a table’s species names as the names a model learnt: the release’s name table, the resolver, the setting a load or a suite prediction takes, and the report of the names not found as written. Species names a model knows by another name walks through it.

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

resolve_names() 

resolve_names(names, model, target=None, table=True, max_edit_distance=1)

Resolves a list of species names against a model’s vocabulary and returns a pandas.DataFrame, one row per name in order: name, token (the name the model reads), route, source, via, distance. model is a SuitePredictor with target, a Predictor, or a vocabulary as a checkpoint orders it ("<UNK>" first). table is the path of the release’s names.json or a NameTable; None or True resolves against the vocabulary alone. Each name takes the first route that reaches a token:

  • exact: the vocabulary holds the name as written;
  • alias: the name table maps the name to a token the vocabulary holds, source naming what linked them (eva for the names EVA’s records were entered under, else the backbone, e.g. wfo);
  • spelling: within max_edit_distance edits (Damerau-Levenshtein, letter case ignored) of a token or a table name whose token the vocabulary holds, searched within the name’s genus first and across every name only when the genus holds none, and used only when every nearest name stands for one species; via is the name it was read through and distance the edits;
  • unresolved: none of these; the name stays as written and counts as a species the model does not know.

At one edit, misspelled copies of the example plots’ names resolved 99.5% to the right species and none to a wrong one; two edits also renamed some species the models never saw, so 1 is the default.

import resolve_core as rc

vocabulary = ["<UNK>", "Quercus robur", "Anemone altaica"]
table = rc.NameTable.from_columns(["Anemone nemorosa"], ["Anemone altaica"], ["eva"])
rc.resolve_names(["Quercus robru", "Anemone nemorosa", "Poa annua"], vocabulary, table=table)

NameTable 

NameTable.open(path)
NameTable.read(path)
NameTable.from_columns(names, tokens, sources)

The release’s name table: each name a user may write for a species, the token it stands for, and the source that linked them. open reads a names.json ({"source": ..., "aliases": {name: [token, source]}}) once per process and hands later callers the same table while the file keeps its size and modification time; read reads it again every time. find(name) returns (token, source) or None; len(table), name in table, description and sha256 (of the file read) describe it.

SpeciesNames 

SpeciesNames(table=None, max_edit_distance=1)

How a load or a suite prediction resolves species names: the NameTable (None: the vocabulary alone) and the edits a misspelling may be away (0 turns the spelling step off). SuitePredictor.predict(names=...) builds one from a path, a NameTable or True; the *_with_vocabs loaders of ResolveDataset take one as names.

NameResolver 

NameResolver(vocabulary, table=None, max_edit_distance=1)

Resolves names against one vocabulary. resolve(name) returns a ResolvedName, resolve_batch(names) a list of them. The spelling index is built on the first name that needs it.

ResolvedName

What the resolver gives for one name: token, route (a NameRoute), source, via and distance.

NameRoute

Exact, Alias, Spelling or Unresolved.

SpeciesNameReport

The species names a load or a suite target did not find as written, one row per name in the order they first appear: name, token, route (as text), source, via, distance and n_records, the records that carried the name. ResolveDataset.species_names and SuiteTargetPrediction.species_names return one; to_pandas() gives it as a data frame.
